_comment: Source spec for the Hanyu Library. Every text here is in the PUBLIC DOMAIN.
The bar is life + 70 years, so the library is clear for worldwide App Store
distribution rather than only in life+50 territories. `pdBasis` records why
each book qualifies; `sourceNote` records where the text came from.
Deliberately EXCLUDED: the erotic classics carried by the same sources
(金瓶梅, 肉蒲團 and the 禁書 series) — wrong fit for the App Store age rating.
as nested lists, matched in SOURCE order not spec order), or 'auto'.
expectChapters is a QA assertion only — it never changes the output.

books.title: 呐喊
books.author: 鲁迅
books.blurb: The collection that founded modern Chinese fiction. Early vernacular 白话 — the first classic you can actually read without translating from Classical Chinese.
books.pdBasis: Lu Xun died 1936; public domain under life+70 since 2007.
books._note: This source edition omits the preface and 頭髮的故事; 13 pieces are present.

books.title: 朝花夕拾
books.author: 鲁迅
books.blurb: Lu Xun's childhood memoirs — warmer and gentler than his fiction, and some of the most approachable prose of the era.
books.pdBasis: Lu Xun died 1936; public domain under life+70 since 2007.
books._note: This source edition carries 8 of the 12 essays; the other four are absent from it entirely.

books.title: 沉沦
books.author: 郁达夫
books.blurb: A landmark of confessional modern fiction, written in plain vernacular Chinese.
books.pdBasis: Yu Dafu died 1945; public domain under life+70 since 2016.

books.title: 欧游杂记
books.author: 朱自清
books.blurb: Travel essays by a master of clear, unfussy modern prose — widely used in Chinese schools as a model of good writing.
books.pdBasis: Zhu Ziqing died 1948; public domain under life+70 since 2019.

books.title: 唐诗三百首
books.author: 蘅塘退士 编
books.blurb: The verses every Chinese child learns by heart. Short, famous and endlessly quotable — the friendliest way into classical Chinese.
books.pdBasis: Compiled 1763; long out of copyright worldwide.

books.title: 诗经
books.author: 佚名
books.blurb: The oldest anthology of Chinese poetry and one of the Five Classics — folk songs, court hymns and ritual odes.
books.pdBasis: Ancient text; long out of copyright worldwide.

books.title: 李太白集
books.author: 李白
books.blurb: China's most beloved poet, in full. Moonlight, wine, exile and the road home.
books.pdBasis: Li Bai died 762; long out of copyright worldwide.
books._noteVariants: 〔校〕/〔注〕 apparatus is deliberate and kept; only the 4 inline in-verse citations are stripped.

books.title: 论语
books.author: 孔子及弟子
books.blurb: The sayings of Confucius, in twenty books. Classical Chinese — read it with the parallel translation alongside.
books.pdBasis: Ancient text; long out of copyright worldwide.

books.title: 道德经
books.author: 老子
books.blurb: Eighty-one short chapters, the foundation of Taoism. Each one is a few lines long — ideal for reading a chapter a day.
books.pdBasis: Ancient text; long out of copyright worldwide.
books.chapterRegex: ^第[一二三四五六七八九十百]+章

books.title: 孙子兵法
books.author: 孙武
books.blurb: Thirteen chapters on strategy — the most quoted Chinese book in the world, and short enough to finish.
books.pdBasis: Ancient text; long out of copyright worldwide.

books.title: 孟子
books.author: 孟子
books.blurb: The second great Confucian text, and a far livelier read than the Analects — Mencius argues, needles and tells stories.
books.pdBasis: Ancient text; long out of copyright worldwide.
books._note: This source edition is a continuous stream with no book/chapter headings, so it is split into even reading sections rather than mislabelled as the traditional seven books.

books.title: 聊斋志异
books.titleEnglish: Strange Tales from a Chinese Studio
books.author: 蒲松龄
books.blurb: Ghost stories, fox spirits and scholars who fall in love with the wrong things. Hundreds of very short tales — dip in anywhere.
books.pdBasis: Pu Songling died 1715; long out of copyright worldwide.

books.title: 古文观止
books.author: 吴楚材、吴调侯 编
books.authorEnglish: compiled by Wu Chucai and Wu Diaohou
books.blurb: The standard anthology of classical prose for three centuries — the essays educated Chinese readers were expected to know.
books.pdBasis: Compiled 1695; long out of copyright worldwide.

books.title: 三字经
books.author: 王应麟
books.blurb: The classic children's primer: the whole of Confucian learning in rhyming three-character lines. Short, rhythmic and made to be memorised.
books.pdBasis: 13th-century text; long out of copyright worldwide.
books._note: Correctly a single continuous text — it is one unbroken rhyming primer, not a chaptered work.

books.title: 庄子
books.author: 庄子
books.blurb: The other great Daoist book, and the funnier one. Butterflies, useless trees and giant fish — Zhuangzi argues by story rather than by maxim, which makes him the most readable of the ancient philosophers.
books.pdBasis: 4th-century BC text; long out of copyright worldwide.
books._note: Chapter order comes from the index page: 7 inner, 15 outer, 11 miscellaneous.

books.title: 墨子
books.author: 墨子及弟子
books.blurb: Confucianism's great rival: universal love, plain living and a hard-headed case against war. Mozi argues like an engineer, and his school built siege defences to prove it.
books.pdBasis: 5th-century BC text; long out of copyright worldwide.
books._note: 53 of the traditional 71 chapters survive; the source carries the surviving set.

books.title: 韩非子
books.author: 韩非
books.blurb: The masterwork of Legalism, and the book that armed China's first emperor. Cold, brilliant and full of parables — this is where 守株待兔 and many other idioms come from.
books.pdBasis: 3rd-century BC text; long out of copyright worldwide.

books.title: 孝经
books.author: 曾子及门人
books.authorEnglish: Attributed to Zengzi and his school
books.blurb: The short classic behind 孝 — filial piety — set out as a conversation between Confucius and his student Zengzi. Eighteen tiny chapters; the whole book is a single sitting.
books.pdBasis: Pre-Han text; long out of copyright worldwide.
books.chapterRegex: ^.{1,8}章第[一二三四五六七八九十]+$
books._note: Free: it is short, and it is the text behind the Filial Piety card in Philosophy.

books.title: 大学·中庸
books.titleEnglish: The Great Learning & The Doctrine of the Mean
books.author: 朱熹 编注
books.blurb: The two short books that complete the Four Books alongside the Analects and the Mencius. Zhu Xi paired them in 1190 and they became the syllabus of imperial China for seven centuries.
books.pdBasis: Pre-Han texts in Zhu Xi's 12th-century edition; long out of copyright worldwide.
books._note: One book from two source texts — a reader wants the Four Books together, not two stubs.

books.title: 史记
books.author: 司马迁
books.blurb: The foundation of Chinese history writing — 130 chapters covering 2,000 years, written by a man who chose disgrace over death to finish it. Reads like biography, not chronicle.
books.pdBasis: 1st-century BC text; long out of copyright worldwide.
books._note: This edition repeats three chapter names (呂后本紀 is headed 高祖本紀); left as the source has it.

books.title: 杜工部集
books.titleEnglish: The Collected Poems of Du Fu
books.author: 杜甫
books.blurb: The complete poems of the 詩聖, the Poet Sage — over a thousand of them, from the early mountain poems to the late exile verse. The other half of Chinese poetry's greatest pairing.
books.pdBasis: 8th-century poems; long out of copyright worldwide.
books.sourceNote: Public-domain text from the 全唐詩 (1705), re-typeset for Hanyu.
books._note: Sourced from Du Fu's own 19 juan in the 全唐詩 (216-234); the 杜工部集 pages on Wikisource are mostly unwritten. Variant readings (一作「X」) and editorial notes are stripped — this is a reading edition, not a critical one.

books.title: 楚辞
books.author: 屈原、宋玉等
books.authorEnglish: Qu Yuan, Song Yu and others
books.blurb: China's other poetic root, beside the Book of Songs — shamanic, southern and strange. Its author Qu Yuan drowned himself in the Miluo, and the Dragon Boat Festival still commemorates him.
books.pdBasis: Ancient text with Han-era commentary; long out of copyright worldwide.
books._note: Explicit page list: the 17 juan are split between standalone pages and 楚辭/ subpages, so neither a prefix crawl nor the index links alone find them all. Each juan opens with Wang Yi's Han commentary preface.

books.title: 古诗十九首
books.author: 佚名
books.blurb: Nineteen anonymous Han poems about separation, time and homesickness — the bridge between the Book of Songs and Tang poetry. Plain five-character lines, and the easiest classical verse to start with.
books.pdBasis: 2nd-century poems; long out of copyright worldwide.
books._note: Free: it is nineteen short poems and the gentlest way into classical verse.

books.title: 漱玉词
books.author: 李清照
books.blurb: The collected ci of China's greatest woman poet. Early poems of wine and plum blossom; later ones written after war took her husband, her home and her collection. Song lyrics, so the rhythm is looser and closer to speech than Tang verse.
books.pdBasis: 12th-century poems; long out of copyright worldwide.
